claim: Asymmetric eligibility collapse makes the benchmark comparison, and the 365-day forward verdict, hostage to a data-vendor holiday gap. Unlike H404701 (board S7: both legs held the same 5 funds, so active could only shrink), here the legs DIVERGE: when <5 funds are rankable the banded candidate skips the decision and keeps its old ~70-fund book (cef_classes.py:279-280), while the benchmark rebalances into the 5 surviving funds (cef_classes.py:136-141). In Jan 2016 (CEFConnect reported 4 and 5 funds on Fridays 2015-12-25 and 2016-01-01; eligible = CEF, KF, PHYS, PSLV, SPPP on 2016-01-04..07) 4 of 21 benchmark tranches (0, 18, 19, 20) held three Sprott metal trusts + CEF + KF for ~21 sessions: ledger active 2016-01-04..02-12 = -1.92% (-3.8% of the whole 22.7-year active sum, ~85% of one year's +2.25% net). Those 4 tranches' active Sharpe is 1.14-1.27 vs 1.75-1.79 with that window removed (all other tranches 1.57-2.00). Both 2026-12-25 and 2027-01-01 are Fridays, inside the forward window that is meant to decide the claim: if CEFConnect repeats 2015-16 (it did not in 2020-21: 303 funds reported), ~19% of the benchmark becomes a metals/2-fund bet against the candidate for a month, a swing of the same size as the expected annual active. The development-sample number is biased AGAINST the candidate (gold rallied in Q1 2016), so this is not inflation; it is an uncontrolled, sign-unknown shock to the forward test and a measurement error in the registered benchmark.

claim: The z52_cat edge is a short-lived (weeks) signal, so the net result is fragile to any implementation or NAV-publication delay, far more than H404701's. Approximate replication (corr 0.993 with the ledger active, gross Sharpe 1.97, +3.18%/yr gross) with the z-score lagged k sessions (eligibility unchanged): k=1 Sharpe 1.81 (+2.93%/yr), k=5 1.45 (+2.38%/yr), k=10 1.24 (+2.03%/yr), k=21 0.84 (+1.39%/yr), k=63 0.31 (+0.52%/yr, t 1.48). Against the candidate's ~1.0%/yr excess cost over the benchmark (ledger 1.09% vs 0.095%/yr), a one-week delay leaves ~+1.4%/yr net and a one-month delay ~+0.4%/yr. Contrast: H404701's level signal kept 62% of its gross edge with a 252-session lag (refuter2 O5). The registered result therefore rests on acting at the next close after each Friday NAV (decision on the Friday-dated observation, panel.as_of at cef_data.py:69-72); any fund whose CEFConnect Friday NAV is in fact published or corrected later than the next session, or a forward/paper process that batches weekly, erodes the edge at roughly 0.15%/yr per session of delay in the first week. The 5.75x/yr turnover is the cost of chasing this decay; the break-even cost multiple is ~3.1x the tier (vs ~6.7x for H404701).

claim: The deflation pass is carried by TODAY's category labels, and only through variance reduction, so point-in-time label quality is load-bearing for the registered metric (active DSR vs SR0 0.94). Same banded rule, approximate replication (gross, corr 0.993 with ledger): true CEFConnect labels Sharpe 1.97 (+3.18%/yr); NO categories 1.20 (+3.10%/yr); labels shuffled across funds (sizes preserved, 10 draws) 1.09-1.25, mean 1.20 (+3.00-3.29%/yr); 4 broad groups (muni / taxable FI / hybrid / equity) 1.76 (+2.97%/yr). The mean return is the same with meaningless labels; the labels only cut tracking error from ~2.6% to ~1.6%/yr. Netting the ~1.0%/yr excess cost, uninformative labels give net active Sharpe ~0.8 (below SR0 0.94, i.e. the DSR would fail); broad, near-unambiguous groups give ~1.17. So the fine-label share of the Sharpe (1.76 -> 1.97 gross) is what cannot be verified point-in-time. Measured bound, for the board: a mandate-drift screen (fund NAV-return correlation with its category median 2003-10 vs 2019-26) flags 11 of 230 long-history funds (ETJ, FMY, GCV, KYN, MIN, MMT, PPT, SPE, SRV, TSI, TYG); they carry 3.2% of the within-category selection return (1.2% in 2004-12) and excluding them leaves selection Sharpe 2.36 vs 2.39, so the detectable leak is small. The threat stands as: the risk-adjusted claim depends on 26 fine labels whose historical accuracy is assumed, not tested beyond this screen.
